chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Khalid ibn Nafi', the seller of Al-Sabiri, from Yusuf Al-Bazzaz, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whenever two people dispute over a matter, and one of them gives half to his companion, he does not accept it from him unless he is given more than him (to be just to him).'

key_terms.أُدِيلَ: to be given justice or treated fairly/equitably
key_terms.تَدَارَأَ: to dispute or contend with each other

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ethical ruling on accepting half in a dispute to settle matters?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of *Udail* (superior equity), warning that accepting a mere half-settlement in a dispute may result in the acceptor being shortchanged if the true value exceeds that amount. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on substantive justice over formal compromise, ensuring that the rights of both parties are fully protected against hidden inequities. It serves as a practical guideline for financial and legal settlements, prioritizing complete fairness to prevent future grievances.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Khalid Bin Nafi’e Baya’a Al Sabiry, from Yusuf Al Bazzaz who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘No two would dispute regarding a matter at all, so one of them gives the half to his companion, but he does not accept from it, except he would be more just than him’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Khalid ibn Nafi’ Bayya’ al-Sabiri from Yusuf al- Bazzaz who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) say, ‘If two people disagree in something, one of them gives half as much to his companion, but if he would not accept, it will be compensated for him (recipient of more than half for his injustice).’”
